newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: GOLF - Singapore tune-up for Eisenhower golfers.
newsitem.headline: GOLF - Singapore tune-up for Eisenhower golfers.

text.p: New Zealand's Eisenhower golf team will use this week's Singapore Amateur Open to put the finishing touches to their world championship campaign.
The team of Richard Hislop (Wellington), Richard Best (Palmerston North), and Aucklanders David Somervaille and Simon Bittle, left New Zealand today, NZPA reported.
Under the guidance of coach Mal Tongue, the team will use the 72-hole Singapore event to acclimatise for the world amateur teams championship which will be played in Manila next month.
At the same time, however, Tongue wants to see all four players not only make the second-round cut but also be in the running for the title.
"I would be disappointed if they didn't consistently break 80," he said.
Tongue was pleased with the team's development during a five-day training camp which ended last week.
"Going to Singapore, for me, is a good thing as I will be able to watch the players in the conditions they will be play in Manila," he said.
Hislop, who will be playing Singapore for the first time, said the tournament was important in that he would be able to fully prepare himself for Manila.
"If you can get yourself in good shape for those conditions, then the golf takes care of itself."
Hislop said Singapore would also provide the chance to play against some of the players who will also be contesting the Eisenhower Trophy.
